papers.title: SurgEye: Instruction Tuning-Free Perception-Reasoning Framework for Surgical Scene Understanding
papers.abstract_en: Surgical scene understanding is pivotal for computer-assisted intervention, yet demands compositional reasoning across instruments, anatomy, and workflow. Existing surgical vision-language models rely on instruction tuning with large-scale question-answer pairs, entailing laborious data curation and costly retraining. To bridge this gap, we propose SurgEye, a perception-reasoning framework that grounds reasoning in a vision foundation model without instruction tuning. Specifically, we devise Routed Multi-Task Perception (RMP) that routes the vision foundation model through task-specific pathways learned from public perception labels, producing spatial and temporal evidence. We further introduce Agentic Compositional Reasoning (ACR) that employs a frozen large language model to coordinate RMP specialists and temporal memory as callable tools, composing evidence across tasks and time into grounded answers. Moreover, we construct SurgEye-Bench spanning eight surgical procedures, pairing each question with perception labels for verifiable evaluation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SurgEye outperforms state-of-the-arts in surgical reasoning. The source code will be available.
papers.abstract_zh: 手术场景理解对计算机辅助干预至关重要，但需要在器械、解剖结构和工作流之间进行组合推理。现有的手术视觉语言模型依赖使用大规模问答对进行指令微调，这带来了繁琐的数据整理和昂贵的重新训练。为弥补这一差距，我们提出 SurgEye，一个无需指令微调、将推理建立在视觉基础模型之上的感知-推理框架。具体而言，我们设计了路由多任务感知（RMP），它通过从公开感知标签中学习到的任务特定路径来路由视觉基础模型，产生空间和时间证据。我们进一步引入智能体组合推理（ACR），它使用一个冻结的大语言模型来协调 RMP 专家和时间记忆作为可调用工具，将跨任务和跨时间的证据组合成有依据的答案。此外，我们构建了涵盖八种手术流程的 SurgEye-Bench，为每个问题配以感知标签以进行可验证评估。大量实验表明，SurgEye 在手术推理方面优于最先进方法。源代码将公开。
papers.tldr_zh: SurgEye 提出无需指令微调的手术场景理解框架，通过路由多任务感知生成空间与时间证据，并用冻结大语言模型协调专家与时间记忆进行组合推理，在八种手术流程的基准上优于现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, foundation model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：state-of-the-art, extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: MonoLaDN: Language-Guided DeNoising for Monocular 3D Object Detection
papers.abstract_en: Monocular 3D object detection offers a low-cost route to 3D perception, but it remains fundamentally ill-posed, since depth must be inferred from a single view. Recent transformer-based detectors learn geometry purely from image features and 3D box annotations, lacking the high-level semantic priors that vision-language models (VLMs) acquire from large-scale pretraining. VLMs offer such priors, but deploying one directly as a detector is impractical due to its heavy inference cost. We propose MonoLaDN, a language-guided denoising framework that transfers the geometric reasoning of a VLM into a monocular 3D detector while keeping the deployed model purely vision-based. During training, a frozen VLM produces structured reasoning about each object's occlusion, depth, dimension, and angle from the image and its ground-truth boxes. We encode this reasoning into queries, perturb them with noise, and train the detector to reconstruct the clean reasoning. Reconstructing the corrupted reasoning forces the detector's depth-guided features to internalize the VLM's geometric priors, so this knowledge remains available even after the reasoning path is discarded at inference, adding no latency or parameters to the deployed model. Experiments on KITTI 3D and nuScenes show that MonoLaDN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art detectors and generalizes well to new domains.
papers.abstract_zh: 单目3D目标检测为3D感知提供了一条低成本路径，但由于深度必须从单一视角推断，该问题本质上是不适定的。近期基于Transformer的检测器仅从图像特征和3D框标注中学习几何信息，缺乏视觉语言模型（VLM）从大规模预训练中获得的高层语义先验。VLM可提供此类先验，但因其推理开销大，直接将其部署为检测器并不现实。我们提出MonoLaDN，一种语言引导的去噪框架，将VLM的几何推理能力迁移到单目3D检测器中，同时使部署模型保持纯视觉。训练时，一个冻结的VLM根据图像及其真值框，对每个目标的遮挡、深度、尺寸和角度生成结构化推理。我们将该推理编码为查询，对其施加噪声扰动，并训练检测器重建干净的推理。重建被破坏的推理迫使检测器的深度引导特征内化VLM的几何先验，因此即使在推理阶段丢弃推理路径，这些知识仍然可用，且不为部署模型增加任何延迟或参数。在KITTI 3D和nuScenes上的实验表明，MonoLaDN持续优于最先进的检测器，并能很好地泛化到新领域。
papers.tldr_zh: MonoLaDN在训练时用冻结VLM生成的结构化几何推理经加噪后训练检测器重建，使纯视觉单目3D检测器内化VLM几何先验，推理时无额外开销，在KITTI 3D和nuScenes上优于现有方法。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Amortized Nonlinear Variable Selection with Prior-Data Fitted Networks
papers.abstract_en: Variable selection is an important task for interpreting potentially complex systems in fields such as biology, business, and sociology. The importance of variable selection has attracted considerable attention in statistics and machine learning. In this paper, we are mainly interested in model-agnostic variable selection for identifying variables that have general nonlinear dependence on the response. We propose MambaPFN, short for Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks, which is built upon the Transformer, a building block of many popular large language models. Specifically, we consider a functional-mapping perspective on variable-selection learning, in which the Transformer is treated as a learnable mapping from a dataset to its relevant variables. To learn this mapping, MambaPFN introduces three new components: (i) a faithful, rich, and scalable scheme for generating pretraining data, (ii) an objective that targets each variable's posterior inclusion probability, and (iii) a modified Transformer architecture tailored to variable selection. Once pretrained, MambaPFN is applied to new datasets without parameter updates. Empirically, MambaPFN achieves desirable variable-selection performance in simulation studies and exhibits a scaling law---more pretraining datasets and larger models can continuously improve its performance. Applied to a Facebook comments dataset, MambaPFN selects the fewest variables and achieves the highest computational efficiency and predictive performance, improving upon the best baselines by about 20%.
papers.abstract_zh: 变量选择是解释生物学、商业和社会学等领域中潜在复杂系统的一项重要任务。变量选择的重要性在统计学和机器学习领域引起了广泛关注。本文主要关注模型无关的变量选择，用于识别与响应变量具有一般非线性依赖关系的变量。我们提出 MambaPFN，即基于先验数据拟合网络的模型无关马尔可夫毯选择（Model-Agnostic Markov BlAnket selection with Prior-data Fitted Networks），它建立在 Transformer 之上，而 Transformer 是许多流行大语言模型的基本构件。具体而言，我们从函数映射的视角看待变量选择学习，将 Transformer 视为从数据集到其相关变量的可学习映射。为学习这一映射，MambaPFN 引入了三个新组件：（i）一种忠实、丰富且可扩展的预训练数据生成方案，（ii）一个以每个变量的后验包含概率为目标的目标函数，以及（iii）一种为变量选择量身定制的改进 Transformer 架构。预训练后，MambaPFN 无需参数更新即可应用于新数据集。在实证上，MambaPFN 在模拟研究中取得了理想的变量选择性能，并展现出缩放规律——更多预训练数据集和更大模型可以持续提升其性能。应用于 Facebook 评论数据集时，MambaPFN 选择的变量最少，并实现了最高的计算效率和预测性能，较最佳基线提升约 20%。
papers.tldr_zh: MambaPFN 将 Transformer 视为从数据集到相关变量的可学习映射，通过预训练数据生成、后验包含概率目标和改进架构实现无需参数更新的模型无关非线性变量选择，并在 Facebook 评论数据集上以最少变量取得最高效率与预测性能。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model, transformer
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
匹配 模型架构：transformer architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes
papers.abstract_en: Existing reasoning segmentation frameworks typically employ multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with broad world knowledge to extract semantics in a human-like manner and generate corresponding segmentation masks. Nevertheless, these frameworks lack the necessary scene-specific awareness. This paper introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation (DSRS), a scene-specific task that requires models to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect potential risks, handle challenging conditions, and comprehend underlying traffic rules, ultimately generating accurate segmentation masks. Meanwhile, we establish a benchmark dataset to facilitate future research on the DSRS task. To pioneer this task, we propose DSRS-Net, a novel architecture with advanced reasoning segmentation capability for automated driving. Specifically, DSRS-Net seamlessly infuses geometric features for deeper reasoning segmentation, without compromising the original multimodal fusion mechanism. This strategy effectively mitigates the modality representation mismatch in MLLMs caused by RGB-only pretraining, while enhancing the integration of geometric, contextual, and linguistic features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DSRS-Net in both driving scene reasoning segmentation and other language-driven segmentation tasks across various public datasets. The source code and dataset will be released upon publication.
papers.abstract_zh: 现有的推理分割框架通常采用具备广泛世界知识的多模态大语言模型（MLLM），以类人的方式提取语义并生成相应的分割掩码。然而，这些框架缺乏必要的场景特定感知能力。本文提出驾驶场景推理分割（DSRS），这是一个场景特定任务，要求模型解读隐式指令、推断空间关系、检测潜在风险、处理挑战性条件并理解底层交通规则，最终生成准确的分割掩码。同时，我们建立了一个基准数据集以促进DSRS任务的未来研究。为开创该任务，我们提出DSRS-Net，一种面向自动驾驶、具备先进推理分割能力的新架构。具体而言，DSRS-Net在不损害原有多模态融合机制的前提下，无缝注入几何特征以实现更深入的推理分割。该策略有效缓解了MLLM因仅RGB预训练导致的模态表示不匹配，同时增强了几何、上下文和语言特征的整合。大量实验表明，DSRS-Net在驾驶场景推理分割及多个公开数据集上的其他语言驱动分割任务中均表现优异。源代码和数据集将在论文发表后发布。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文提出驾驶场景推理分割任务DSRS并构建基准数据集，提出DSRS-Net在保持多模态融合机制的同时注入几何特征，缓解RGB预训练导致的模态表示不匹配，在驾驶场景推理分割等任务上表现优异。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Library of Layers (LoL): Adaptively Ordering Transformer Layers at Runtime
papers.abstract_en: Computer programmers chain together the same reusable computational primitives, for example, conditional statements or loops, but in different orders to implement different algorithms. In contrast, existing language model architectures always execute their layers in the same order. We introduce Library of Layers (LoL), an architecture that dynamically orders its layers during inference to solve the problem at hand. LoL has a single hyperparameter, the size of its global library of transformer blocks, that allows it to transition seamlessly between parameter reuse and sparsity, generalizing the parameter-efficiency and FLOPs-efficiency tradeoffs of dense, depth-recurrent, and mixture of experts architectures in one unified family. We show that LoL achieves competitive performance with all three above baselines when pretrained on text data. On synthetic sudoku and maze data, we observe that the model employs distinct layer orderings to implement different solution strategies, and we can intervene on routing to force a model to apply a specific solution strategy to a problem instance. In a multilingual natural language setting, we find that LoL chooses different layer order patterns based on language and script. Similarly, we train LoL on safety data and fit probes to its router outputs, finding that these probes distinguish safe from unsafe text with high AUROC. LoL provides a path toward a future in which models dynamically compose their own computational graph, enabling more efficient and controllable reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 计算机程序员将相同的可复用计算原语（例如条件语句或循环）以不同顺序串联，以实现不同算法。相比之下，现有语言模型架构总是以相同顺序执行其层。我们提出 Library of Layers（LoL），一种在推理时动态排序其层以解决当前问题的架构。LoL 只有一个超参数，即其全局 transformer 块库的大小，使其能在参数复用与稀疏性之间无缝转换，将稠密、深度循环和混合专家架构的参数效率与 FLOPs 效率权衡统一到一个家族中。我们表明，在文本数据上预训练时，LoL 与上述三种基线均取得有竞争力的性能。在合成的数独和迷宫数据上，我们观察到模型采用不同的层排序来实现不同的求解策略，并且我们可以干预路由以强制模型对某个问题实例应用特定求解策略。在多语言自然语言设定中，我们发现 LoL 根据语言和文字选择不同的层排序模式。类似地，我们在安全数据上训练 LoL 并对其路由器输出拟合探针，发现这些探针能以高 AUROC 区分安全与不安全文本。LoL 为模型动态组合自身计算图、实现更高效可控推理的未来提供了一条路径。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 Library of Layers（LoL）架构，在推理时动态排序共享的 transformer 块库，以单一超参数统一稠密、深度循环与混合专家架构的效率权衡，并在数独、迷宫、多语言和安全任务中观察到与任务相关的层排序模式。
why_it_matters: 匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: GroundSeek-CXR: Retrospective Evaluation-Guided Active Observation Framework for Multi-Label Chest Radiography Diagnosis
papers.abstract_en: Chest radiography (CXR) diagnosis is critical for thoracic disease assessment, yet challenged by the need to identify subtle lesions and co-occurring abnormalities across regions. While recent vision-language models can actively observe local regions, existing preference-based methods supervise each observation by its immediate effect on the current diagnosis, failing to capture how each observation and stopping decision contributes to the final diagnosis. To address this issue, we propose GroundSeek-CXR, an active CXR diagnosis framework that learns observation and stopping decisions by retrospectively evaluating them with the final diagnosis. Specifically, we first devise a Retrospective Diagnostic Evaluation (RDE) that scores observation and stop candidates from offline Monte Carlo tree search through independent continuations. Moreover, we design a Retrospective Gap-weighted Preference Optimization (RGPO) that learns from retrospective-score preferences weighted by their score gaps, prioritizing actions that improve diagnostic accuracy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our GroundSeek-CXR framework outperforms state-of-the-art methods, and improves abnormal-image sample-F1 by 4.48% over immediate-score preference learning.
papers.abstract_zh: 胸部 X 线摄影（CXR）诊断对胸部疾病评估至关重要，但面临识别跨区域细微病灶和共现异常的挑战。尽管近期视觉语言模型能够主动观察局部区域，但现有基于偏好的方法以每次观察对当前诊断的即时效果来监督每次观察，未能捕捉每次观察和停止决策如何贡献于最终诊断。为解决这一问题，我们提出 GroundSeek-CXR，一个主动 CXR 诊断框架，通过用最终诊断回溯评估观察和停止决策来学习它们。具体而言，我们首先设计回溯诊断评估（RDE），通过独立延续从离线蒙特卡洛树搜索中为观察和停止候选打分。此外，我们设计回溯差距加权偏好优化（RGPO），从按分数差距加权的回溯分数偏好中学习，优先考虑提升诊断准确性的动作。大量实验表明，我们的 GroundSeek-CXR 框架优于最先进方法，并将异常图像样本 F1 较即时分数偏好学习提升 4.48%。
papers.tldr_zh: GroundSeek-CXR 用最终诊断回溯评估观察与停止决策，通过蒙特卡洛树搜索打分和差距加权偏好优化学习主动观察策略，在胸部 X 线多标签诊断中优于现有方法并将异常图像样本 F1 提升 4.48%。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：preference optimization
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：state-of-the-art, extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether vision-language models (VLMs) can enable page-native deep research: directly retrieving and reasoning over rendered document page images. We introduce DR Pixel, the first open-source end-to-end multimodal DR agent that uses rendered page images as its sole retrieval and reasoning unit, operating over a corpus of 1.06M pages. To evaluate this setting, we construct DRPixelBench, a benchmark on scientific papers requiring reasoning over text, figures, tables, and equations. Surprisingly, page-native DR already works well without training, outperforming OCR-based baselines across state-of-the-art models like GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B, while requiring fewer tool calls. We next turn to DR training. A key challenge is that teacher trajectories for agentic supervised finetuning are noisy, mixing critical reasoning and action steps with redundant or failed attempts. To address this, we introduce counterfactual credit reweighting, a fine-grained credit assignment method that weights individual reasoning and action steps by their counterfactual contribution to the final answer. Our training improves retrieval recall by about 15 points and final accuracy by over 10 points on DRPixelBench, and likewise outperforms the untrained baseline on four existing benchmarks. On out-of-distribution ViDoRe-V3, DR Pixel comes within 1.8 points of an oracle that is given the gold pages directly. Our results suggest that the conventional OCR-then-retrieve pipeline is not only unnecessary but suboptimal: directly retrieving and reasoning over visual document pages makes complex DR both more effective and more efficient.
papers.abstract_zh: 科学论文等复杂文档在表格、图和公式中蕴含丰富信息；然而，现有深度研究（DR）智能体通常将论文简化为 OCR 提取的文本。我们转而探究视觉语言模型（VLM）能否实现页面原生深度研究：直接对渲染的文档页面图像进行检索和推理。我们提出 DR Pixel，首个以渲染页面图像作为唯一检索与推理单元、在 106 万页语料上运行的端到端多模态 DR 智能体。为评估这一设定，我们构建 DRPixelBench，一个要求对文本、图、表和公式进行推理的科学论文基准。令人意外的是，页面原生 DR 在无需训练时已表现良好，在 GPT-5.4、Gemini-3.5-Flash 和 Qwen3.6-27B 等最先进模型上均优于基于 OCR 的基线，且所需工具调用更少。我们随后转向 DR 训练。一个关键挑战是，用于智能体监督微调的教师轨迹含有噪声，混合了关键推理与动作步骤以及冗余或失败尝试。为此，我们引入反事实信用重加权，一种细粒度信用分配方法，按各推理与动作步骤对最终答案的反事实贡献进行加权。我们的训练在 DRPixelBench 上将检索召回率提升约 15 个点、最终准确率提升超过 10 个点，并在四个现有基准上同样优于未训练基线。在分布外 ViDoRe-V3 上，DR Pixel 与直接给定金标页面的 oracle 相差 1.8 个点以内。结果表明，传统的先 OCR 再检索流程不仅不必要而且次优：直接对视觉文档页面进行检索和推理使复杂 DR 更有效也更高效。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出页面原生深度研究智能体 DR Pixel，以渲染页面图像作为唯一检索与推理单元，并引入反事实信用重加权训练方法，在 DRPixelBench 上检索召回率提升约 15 个点、最终准确率提升超过 10 个点，优于基于 OCR 的流程。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Aligning Training and Rollout Policies for End-to-End FP4 RL on Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we study end-to-end FP4 reinforcement learning (RL) post-training for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models. Recent work on FP4 RL has introduced effective recovery recipes that restore accuracy under aggressive low-precision quantization for dense models, but we find that the same approach yields no improvement over the naive FP4 baseline in the MoE setting. We conduct an in-depth study to understand why. Our analysis identifies the root cause in the routing mechanism unique to MoE: because the router makes discrete expert-selection decisions, training-inference policy alignment becomes acutely sensitive to whether the same recovery technique is applied symmetrically on the training and inference sides. When an asymmetric recipe is used-including the dense-model approach, which corrects only the rollout-training-inference alignment deteriorates sharply, as measured by the Pearson correlation coefficient between training and inference probabilities, and router selection matching rates. Building on this finding, we propose MoEResQ, a quantization-recovery recipe for MoE RL post-training that enforces symmetry between the training- and inference-side corrections. MoEResQ restores training-inference alignment and substantially closes the accuracy gap to full precision, establishing symmetric recovery as the key principle in FP4 RL for MoE models.
papers.abstract_zh: 本文研究混合专家（MoE）大语言模型的端到端FP4强化学习（RL）后训练。近期关于FP4 RL的工作提出了有效的恢复方案，可在激进低精度量化下为稠密模型恢复精度，但我们发现相同方法在MoE设定下相比朴素FP4基线并无提升。我们进行了深入研究以理解原因。分析将根因定位在MoE特有的路由机制：由于路由器做出离散的专家选择决策，训练-推理策略对齐对训练侧与推理侧是否对称应用同一恢复技术变得极为敏感。当使用非对称方案时——包括仅校正rollout的稠密模型方法——训练与推理的对齐会急剧恶化，这以训练与推理概率之间的皮尔逊相关系数以及路由器选择匹配率衡量。基于这一发现，我们提出MoEResQ，一种用于MoE RL后训练的量化恢复方案，强制训练侧与推理侧校正之间的对称性。MoEResQ恢复了训练-推理对齐，并大幅缩小了与全精度的精度差距，确立了对称恢复作为MoE模型FP4 RL的关键原则。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文发现MoE模型FP4 RL中非对称量化恢复会因离散路由决策破坏训练-推理对齐，提出对称恢复方案MoEResQ，恢复对齐并大幅缩小与全精度的精度差距。

papers.title: Pixel-space video generation with U-JiT
papers.abstract_en: Latent diffusion and flow matching models are ubiquitous in state-of-the-art generative video models. While highly effective, relying on pretrained autoencoders to compress the data into a lower-dimensional latent space also comes with drawbacks. First, training proceeds in two stages: autoencoder pretraining, with compression and reconstruction objectives, followed by latent generative model training, precluding fully end-to-end training. Second, autoencoders also lead to an inherent loss of signal, and the trade-off between reconstruction quality and generative performance in the latent space is still an active area of research. In this paper we explore the viability of generative video models directly in pixel space. We analyze recent approaches in pixel-space generative modeling of images that rely on basic transformer designs, and identify several shortcomings that limit their effectiveness for the high-dimensional pixel-space video generation. To overcome these limitations, we propose a UNet-like transformer architecture along with improvements to the training recipe and sampling strategy. We conduct controlled experiments, training latent and pixel-space models from scratch on Kinetics-600. For the standard frames-to-video task at 128 resolution, our U-JiT model improves generative FVD by 27% over prior state-of-the-art results, and by 14% against the JiT pixel-space baseline. Scaling to higher 256 resolution, we find the improvement over pixel-space and latent-based models grows as we increase the spatiotemporal compression rate up to $64 \times 64 \times 8$. Finally, we find that U-JiT improves per-frame FID by 27% over latent models and 61% over pixel-space models on class-to-video generation, with respectively 9% and 56% reduction in FVD.
papers.abstract_zh: 潜空间扩散与流匹配模型在当前最先进的生成式视频模型中无处不在。尽管非常有效，依赖预训练自编码器将数据压缩到低维潜空间也带来了缺点。首先，训练分两个阶段进行：先以压缩和重建为目标预训练自编码器，再训练潜空间生成模型，这排除了完全端到端训练的可能。其次，自编码器还会导致固有的信号损失，而潜空间中重建质量与生成性能之间的权衡仍是活跃的研究领域。本文探索直接在像素空间构建生成式视频模型的可行性。我们分析了近期依赖基础 Transformer 设计的图像像素空间生成建模方法，并指出若干限制其在高维像素空间视频生成中有效性的缺陷。为克服这些限制，我们提出一种类 UNet 的 Transformer 架构，并改进训练配方与采样策略。我们在 Kinetics-600 上从头训练潜空间与像素空间模型，进行受控实验。对于 128 分辨率下的标准帧到视频任务，我们的 U-JiT 模型将生成 FVD 较此前最先进结果提升 27%，较 JiT 像素空间基线提升 14%。扩展到更高的 256 分辨率时，我们发现随着时空压缩率提高到 $64 \times 64 \times 8$，相对像素空间和基于潜空间的模型的改进随之增大。最后，我们发现 U-JiT 在类别到视频生成上将逐帧 FID 较潜空间模型提升 27%、较像素空间模型提升 61%，FVD 分别降低 9% 和 56%。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出类 UNet 的 Transformer 架构 U-JiT 直接在像素空间生成视频，并在 Kinetics-600 上较像素空间与潜空间基线取得更优的 FVD 和 FID。

papers.title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to scale capacity efficiently, but expert parameters dominate memory even though only a few experts are activated per token: they account for over 90% of model size in modern MoE-MLLMs (e.g., 54 GB out of about 58 GB in BF16 for InternVL3.5-30B-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B). Expert pruning has emerged as an effective compression strategy, but existing methods aggregate importance uniformly across tokens, ignoring that the same expert may serve different roles for vision versus language processing. To address this, we propose MAEP (Modality-Aware Expert Pruning), a training-free framework that decomposes expert importance by modality in a single forward pass. MAEP introduces (1) Delta-H Output ($ΔH$), a redistribution-aware metric measuring the MoE output change when an expert is removed, and (2) low-attention vision tokens as a vision-side pruning signal that is dataset-stable: its expert-importance ranking remains stable across different datasets. Text-side importance serves as a preservation signal while vision-side importance serves as a pruning signal, and experts are ranked globally across layers. Experiments on three MoE-based MLLMs across multimodal and text benchmarks show that MAEP outperforms modality-agnostic baselines on the majority of multimodal benchmarks while remaining competitive on text-only tasks, reducing the BF16 expert weight footprint by about 27 GB (about 47% of total memory) so that the full weight footprint of an approximately 58 GB model fits within a single 40 GB GPU. Code is available at https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合专家（MoE）使多模态大语言模型（MLLM）能够高效扩展容量，但专家参数主导内存占用，尽管每个token仅激活少数专家：在现代MoE-MLLM中，专家参数占模型规模的90%以上（例如InternVL3.5-30B-A3B和Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B在BF16下约58 GB中的54 GB）。专家剪枝已成为一种有效的压缩策略，但现有方法在所有token上统一聚合重要性，忽略了同一专家在视觉与语言处理中可能承担不同角色。为此，我们提出MAEP（模态感知专家剪枝），一个无需训练的框架，在单次前向传播中按模态分解专家重要性。MAEP引入（1）Delta-H输出（ΔH），一种衡量移除某专家时MoE输出变化的再分配感知指标，以及（2）低注意力视觉token作为视觉侧剪枝信号，该信号具有数据集稳定性：其专家重要性排序在不同数据集间保持稳定。文本侧重要性作为保留信号，视觉侧重要性作为剪枝信号，专家在跨层范围内全局排序。在三个MoE-MLLM上跨多模态和文本基准的实验表明，MAEP在多数多模态基准上优于模态无关基线，同时在纯文本任务上保持竞争力，将BF16专家权重占用减少约27 GB（约占总内存的47%），使约58 GB模型的全部权重可装入单张40 GB GPU。代码见https://github.com/nota-github/MAEP。
papers.tldr_zh: MAEP按模态分解专家重要性，以视觉侧低注意力token为剪枝信号、文本侧为保留信号并跨层全局排序，无需训练即可将MoE-MLLM专家权重减少约27 GB，多模态基准上优于模态无关基线。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: Entropogram-guided Visual Realignment Decoding: Capturing the Rhythm of Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated remarkable progress on cross-modal reasoning tasks, yet they continue to suffer from hallucinations in long-chain reasoning processes. In this work, we revisit hallucination in MLLMs from the perspective of reasoning generation dynamics. We argue that entropy is not merely a static measure of uncertainty but a structured signal that reflects how modality information is integrated throughout decoding. Through systematic analysis, we identify two characteristic entropy patterns associated with hallucination behaviors: (1) a generally high-confidence regime corresponds to premature convergence to inappropriate multimodal interactions; and (2) local abrupt entropy transitions are associated with reasoning instability and hallucination onset. Building on these observations, we propose an entropy-aware self-introspective framework for MLLM reasoning. Our method continuously tracks entropy dynamics during decoding and performs targeted visual re-alignment when suspicious hallucination states are detected, encouraging the model to re-examine salient visual evidence at critical reasoning stages. Extensive experiments across six multimodal reasoning benchmarks spanning nine distinct evaluation settings demonstrate that our approach delivers robust improvements in reasoning accuracy and hallucination robustness, while providing new insights into the generation dynamics underlying MLLM failures. The code is available at: https://github.com/jden4524/SelfRetrospectiveDecoding.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在跨模态推理任务上取得了显著进展，但在长链推理过程中仍存在幻觉问题。本文从推理生成动态的视角重新审视MLLM中的幻觉。我们认为熵不仅是静态的不确定性度量，更是反映模态信息在整个解码过程中如何整合的结构化信号。通过系统分析，我们识别出与幻觉行为相关的两种特征性熵模式：（1）整体高置信度状态对应于过早收敛到不恰当的多模态交互；（2）局部熵的突变与推理不稳定和幻觉发生相关。基于这些观察，我们提出一种面向MLLM推理的熵感知自省框架。该方法在解码过程中持续跟踪熵动态，并在检测到可疑幻觉状态时执行有针对性的视觉重对齐，促使模型在关键推理阶段重新审视显著视觉证据。在涵盖九种不同评估设置的六个多模态推理基准上的大量实验表明，该方法在推理准确性和幻觉鲁棒性上均带来稳健提升，同时为MLLM失败的生成动态提供了新见解。代码见：https://github.com/jden4524/SelfRetrospectiveDecoding。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文从解码熵动态视角分析MLLM幻觉，识别出高置信度过早收敛与局部熵突变两种模式，提出熵感知自省框架在检测到可疑状态时进行视觉重对齐，在六个多模态推理基准上提升准确性与幻觉鲁棒性。

papers.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
papers.abstract_en: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.
papers.abstract_zh: 随着预训练规模扩大，医学语言模型在临床问答方面进展迅速。但其通过持续干预实现有效生理控制的能力仍缺乏系统的定量评估。1 型糖尿病提供了一个具体场景：胰岛素分泌受损导致对外源性胰岛素的依赖，需要依据进餐、运动、疾病和血糖测量信息持续调整剂量。我们提出 DiabAgent，一个面向智能体生理控制的研究套件，包含 Agentic Physiological Control（APC）框架、DiabetSim 模拟器和 SweetBench 基准。APC 通过医疗设备工具控制血糖，利用持续观测推断个体状态、积累个人经验并选择治疗动作。我们构建 DiabetSim 以模拟不同患者、事件和设备条件，用于可扩展的虚拟测试与训练。利用 DiabetSim，我们将 32 个场景设计实例化为 212 个血糖控制任务，构建 SweetBench。在 Claude Opus 5.5 和固定一小时决策间隔下，APC 的 COGI 达到 73.5，而开源闭环基线 OpenAPS 为 71.2。消融进一步表明，个体适应和上下文信息可改善血糖控制。将高频规则控制与较低频智能体决策相结合，显示出平衡控制性能与计算成本的潜力。我们的工作为智能体参与人类生理控制提供了框架、模拟器和评估基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 DiabAgent 套件（APC 框架、DiabetSim 模拟器、SweetBench 基准），在 212 个血糖控制任务上 APC 的 COGI 为 73.5，高于 OpenAPS 的 71.2。

papers.title: Beyond Token Representations: Explicit Visual Object Grounding for Video Reasoning Segmentation
papers.abstract_en: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) aims to infer and segment target objects specified by reasoning queries in videos. Existing methods typically first infer the target and generate a few segmentation tokens for it, which are then fed into a mask decoder for mask prediction. However, such segmentation tokens tend to be both semantically monotonous and spatially ambiguous, making them largely insufficient to represent the target to guide mask prediction. In this paper, we propose an explicit visual object grounding framework for VRS. Specifically, we first propose a spatial-aware prompt generation and refinement scheme, in which we query a multimodal large language model to generate explicit spatial prompts (i.e., bounding box and point set) for the target and then refine them through multi-step dialogue. Furthermore, we introduce a query diversification and alignment module to generate auxiliary queries that describe the same target from different perspectives. We then enforce cross-query consistency between their predicted spatial prompts to alleviate the training bias caused by query limitations. Finally, we select several reliable frames using a prompt-based keyframe selection strategy to support mask decoding and propagation. Extensive experiments on eight datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/viscom-tongji/EVOG.
papers.abstract_zh: 视频推理分割（VRS）旨在推断并分割视频中由推理查询指定的目标对象。现有方法通常先推断目标并为其生成少量分割 token，然后将其送入掩码解码器进行掩码预测。然而，此类分割 token 往往在语义上单调且在空间上模糊，使其在很大程度上不足以表示目标以指导掩码预测。在本文中，我们提出一种用于 VRS 的显式视觉对象定位框架。具体而言，我们首先提出一种空间感知提示生成与细化方案，其中我们查询多模态大语言模型为目标生成显式空间提示（即边界框和点集），然后通过多步对话对其进行细化。此外，我们引入查询多样化与对齐模块，生成从不同视角描述同一目标的辅助查询。然后，我们强制它们预测的空间提示之间的跨查询一致性，以缓解查询局限性造成的训练偏差。最后，我们使用基于提示的关键帧选择策略选择若干可靠帧，以支持掩码解码和传播。在八个数据集上的大量实验表明，我们的方法显著优于最先进方法。代码见 https://github.com/viscom-tongji/EVOG。
papers.tldr_zh: 针对视频推理分割中分割 token 语义单调、空间模糊的问题，提出显式视觉对象定位框架，用多模态大语言模型生成并细化边界框与点集提示、通过查询多样化与跨查询一致性对齐，并在八个数据集上显著优于现有方法。

papers.title: Open-HumanScale: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanScale, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanScale-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanScale-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.
papers.abstract_zh: 第一人称人类视频为机器人学习提供了可扩展的操作先验来源，但将原始数据规模转化为可泛化的机器人策略需要严格的数据整理与训练配方。我们提出 Open-HumanScale，首个将第一人称预训练扩展至 50,000 小时的完全开放配方，其核心是 Open-HumanScale-50K——一个经过整理、密集标注手部运动与自然语言的第一人称视频语料库。基于该语料库，我们通过闭环仿真评估系统性地研究了纯人类预训练，并发现了一个将预训练数据小时数与下游机器人成功率联系起来的经验对数线性缩放定律。基于这些发现，我们开发了 HumanWAM-Vanilla，一个仅使用 50k 小时第一人称人类视频预训练的世界-动作模型。经过机器人后训练后，HumanWAM-Vanilla 在 RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean 上达到 92.08% 的成功率，在 Clean2Random 上达到 68.88%，并在 RoboDojo 上取得 14.17% 的平均成功率和 19.00 的平均进度分数。为进一步推进能力前沿，我们探索了联合人类-机器人预训练，提出 HumanWAM-Goal，一个以视觉目标为条件的世界-动作模型。混合数据缩放解锁了在仿真和物理基准上的广泛零样本泛化能力，将后训练的 RoboTwin 2.0 性能推至新的最先进水平：Clean2Clean 上 92.70%，Clean2Random 上大幅跃升至 84.60%。在物理机器人上，HumanWAM-Goal 进一步展现出涌现的具身上下文学习能力，无需参数更新即可动态调整其操作行为以适应未见过的视觉目标。为支持具身 AI 中可复现的缩放研究，我们开源了 Open-HumanScale-50K 语料库、数据整理与预训练流程，以及预训练和后训练的 HumanWAM 检查点、推理代码和仿真评估套件。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出首个开放的第一人称人类视频预训练配方 Open-HumanScale，构建 50K 小时标注语料并发现数据小时数与机器人成功率的对数线性缩放定律，训练出 HumanWAM-Vanilla 与联合人类-机器人预训练的 HumanWAM-Goal，在 RoboTwin 2.0 等基准上取得领先性能并展现零样本泛化与具身上下文学习。

papers.title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
papers.abstract_en: Static and incomplete parametric knowledge limits the performance of multimodal large language models on novel-knowledge and knowledge-intensive tasks, especially those requiring multi-hop evidence acquisition. Existing multimodal agentic search methods often fix visual evidence at the input or a predefined trajectory position, making it difficult for agents to select search modalities as their information needs evolve and to handle complex real-world queries. We define this capability as autonomous cross-modal search: an agent chooses among direct reasoning, text-to-text search, text-to-image search, and reverse-image search, actively introduces visual evidence when appropriate, and switches between and integrates modalities across multiple hops. We propose ModalSearch-Pipeline, a scalable procedure for constructing an interleaved multimodal knowledge graph. It samples paths with diverse depths and modality compositions and uses backward question construction to obscure entity names and image targets that would expose reasoning shortcuts while retaining necessary disambiguating clues, yielding text-only, image-initialized, and arbitrarily interleaved multi-hop problems. We train the ModalSearcher Agent with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning in a live Web environment, and construct ModalSearch-Bench. Experiments show that ModalSearcher-8B improves average accuracy by 16.2 points over Qwen3-VL-8B under the same agentic workflow across five multimodal knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks, with consistent gains on independently constructed active visual-search benchmarks.
papers.abstract_zh: 静态且不完整的参数化知识限制了多模态大语言模型在新知识和知识密集型任务上的表现，尤其是那些需要多跳证据获取的任务。现有多模态智能体搜索方法通常将视觉证据固定在输入或预定义的轨迹位置，使智能体难以随着信息需求的变化选择搜索模态，也难以处理复杂的现实世界查询。我们将这一能力定义为自主跨模态搜索：智能体在直接推理、文本到文本搜索、文本到图像搜索和反向图像搜索之间进行选择，在适当时主动引入视觉证据，并在多跳过程中切换和整合模态。我们提出 ModalSearch-Pipeline，一种用于构建交错多模态知识图谱的可扩展流程。它采样具有多样深度和模态组成的路径，并使用反向问题构建来遮蔽会暴露推理捷径的实体名称和图像目标，同时保留必要的消歧线索，从而生成纯文本、图像初始化和任意交错的多跳问题。我们在实时 Web 环境中通过监督微调和强化学习训练 ModalSearcher Agent，并构建了 ModalSearch-Bench。实验表明，在相同的智能体工作流下，ModalSearcher-8B 在五个多模态知识密集型问答基准上相较 Qwen3-VL-8B 平均准确率提升 16.2 个百分点，并在独立构建的主动视觉搜索基准上取得一致增益。
papers.tldr_zh: 定义自主跨模态搜索能力并提出 ModalSearch-Pipeline 构建交错多模态知识图谱，训练 ModalSearcher-8B 智能体，在五个多模态知识密集型问答基准上较 Qwen3-VL-8B 平均准确率提升 16.2 个百分点。

papers.title: Q-CamTuning: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Fine-Grained Quality Reasoning in Livestreaming Camera Tuning
papers.abstract_en: With the popularization of livestreaming applications, automatic camera tuning has become indispensable for ordinary users to enjoy high Quality of Experience (QoE). However, the existing Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods face two challenges in camera tuning. First, they struggle to identify subtle quality difference between images, which is common in camera tuning. Second, the ability to explain fine-grained differences and to provide suggestions for camera tuning are even more lacking. To address these challenges, we first construct FGLive-Comments, an instruction tuning dataset with rich annotations of both preferences for fine-grained image pairs and quality reasoning from global and local visual evidence, which supports selective adjustment recommendations of camera parameters. Based on FGLive-Comments, we develop Q-CamTuning, a multimodal large language model for livestreaming camera tuning. Its progressive perception-evidence-guidance framework learns quality-aware visual representations, enhances fine-grained reasoning with global-local evidence, and maps quality issues to camera-parameter adjustment directions. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that Q-CamTuning outperforms existing IQA models in both quality scoring and fine-grained image pair ranking. User study also validates its ability to recommend camera tuning suggestions.
papers.abstract_zh: 随着直播应用的普及，自动摄像头调优已成为普通用户获得高体验质量（QoE）不可或缺的手段。然而，现有图像质量评估（IQA）方法在摄像头调优中面临两个挑战。第一，它们难以识别摄像头调优中常见的图像间细微质量差异。第二，解释细粒度差异并提供摄像头调优建议的能力更加缺乏。为应对这些挑战，我们首先构建了 FGLive-Comments，一个指令调优数据集，包含对细粒度图像对的偏好标注以及基于全局和局部视觉证据的质量推理，支持摄像头参数的选择性调整建议。基于 FGLive-Comments，我们开发了 Q-CamTuning，一个面向直播摄像头调优的多模态大语言模型。其渐进式感知—证据—引导框架学习质量感知的视觉表示，利用全局—局部证据增强细粒度推理，并将质量问题映射到摄像头参数调整方向。大量实验结果表明，Q-CamTuning 在质量评分和细粒度图像对排序上均优于现有 IQA 模型。用户研究也验证了其推荐摄像头调优建议的能力。
papers.tldr_zh: 构建 FGLive-Comments 数据集并提出 Q-CamTuning 多模态大模型，以感知—证据—引导框架在质量评分与细粒度图像对排序上优于现有 IQA 模型。

papers.title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection. It interprets the acquired evidence, updates its plan as needed, and integrates global and local information to generate the final caption. To learn this observation strategy, we develop a verification-guided pipeline that constructs high-quality training trajectories through factual verification and teacher-guided refinement. We further train Reviso using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), incorporating a key-fact reward for caption quality, a Plan Alignment Reward (PAR) for identifying important observation targets, and an Unproductive Tool-Call Penalty (UTCP) that adjusts observation-cost penalties based on caption quality. Experiments across four video captioning benchmarks show that Reviso outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines, while its generated captions better support downstream video question answering. These findings highlight the effectiveness and potential of priority-guided active observation for video captioning.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）能够生成详细的视频描述，但它们可能过度强调次要细节，而忽视关键上下文和关键事件。我们认为并非所有视觉证据都应获得同等关注，因为视觉信息的重要性取决于每个视频的内容。受此观察启发，我们提出 Reviso，一个智能体视频描述框架，学习观察什么以及如何收集相关视觉证据。从低帧率全局预览出发，Reviso 构建分层 Context–Focus–Points（CFP）观察计划，识别视频上下文、优先排序关键方面，并定义具体观察目标和相应工具。在该计划引导下，Reviso 通过选择性重访时间片段并组合工具进行细粒度检查，执行目标导向的主动感知。它解释所获证据，按需更新计划，并整合全局与局部信息以生成最终描述。为学习这一观察策略，我们开发了验证引导的流水线，通过事实核验和教师引导精炼构建高质量训练轨迹。我们进一步使用 Group Relative Policy Optimization（GRPO）训练 Reviso，引入关键事实奖励用于描述质量、Plan Alignment Reward（PAR）用于识别重要观察目标，以及 Unproductive Tool-Call Penalty（UTCP）根据描述质量调整观察成本惩罚。在四个视频描述基准上的实验表明，Reviso 优于所评估的开源基线，其生成的描述也更好地支持下游视频问答。这些发现凸显了优先级引导的主动观察在视频描述中的有效性与潜力。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 Reviso 智能体视频描述框架，以分层 CFP 计划引导主动感知并用 GRPO 训练，在四个基准上优于所评估开源基线且更好支持下游视频问答。

papers.title: PlantVLM-Edge: Quantized Vision-Language Models for On-Device Crop Health Diagnosis
papers.abstract_en: Timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is essential for sustainable agricultural production, yet accurate diagnosis often requires expert knowledge that is not readily available. Recent vision-language models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and natural-language interaction, creating new opportunities for intelligent crop health assessment. However, deploying VLMs on resource-constrained devices remains challenging due to their substantial computational and memory requirements. This paper presents PlantVLM-Edge, a quantized vision-language framework for conversational crop health diagnosis that can run entirely on resource-constrained edge devices. PlantVLM-Edge combines agricultural domain adaptation, post-training quantization, and on-device serving with an offline chat interface, allowing growers to ask open-ended questions and receive diagnoses, symptom explanations, and management guidance without cloud connectivity. The framework is backbone-agnostic: we validate it with two different VLM types with varying scale and architecture (Qwen3-VL-2B and LLaVA-1.5-7B), four quantization schemes, and two diagnostic domains (plant diseases and insect pests), and we deploy all variants on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin. Eight-bit quantization affects answer quality minimally relative to the full-precision model, and 4-bit activation-aware weight quantization (AWQ) retains 98.6% of full-precision answer quality on both domains while reducing the weight memory of the 2B backbone by 49%. In its most compact form, PlantVLM-Edge requires 2.01 GiB of weight memory, returns its first token in about 0.12 s, and completes a 64-token diagnostic response in 0.78 s. These results demonstrate that timely and accurate crop health diagnosis is practical on edge devices, providing a foundation for next-generation crop monitoring and decision support systems.
papers.abstract_zh: 及时、准确的作物健康诊断对可持续农业生产至关重要，但准确诊断往往需要不易获得的专家知识。近期视觉语言模型（VLM）在视觉理解、推理和自然语言交互方面展现出卓越能力，为智能作物健康评估创造了新机遇。然而，由于计算和内存需求巨大，在资源受限设备上部署VLM仍具挑战。本文提出PlantVLM-Edge，一个可完全在资源受限边缘设备上运行的、用于对话式作物健康诊断的量化视觉语言框架。PlantVLM-Edge结合了农业领域自适应、训练后量化和带离线聊天界面的设备端服务，使种植者无需云连接即可提出开放式问题，并获得诊断、症状解释和管理指导。该框架与骨干模型无关：我们使用两种规模和架构不同的VLM（Qwen3-VL-2B和LLaVA-1.5-7B）、四种量化方案和两个诊断领域（植物病害和虫害）进行验证，并将所有变体部署在NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin上。相对于全精度模型，8比特量化对答案质量影响极小，4比特激活感知权重量化（AWQ）在两个领域均保留全精度答案质量的98.6%，同时将2B骨干的权重内存减少49%。在最紧凑形式下，PlantVLM-Edge需要2.01 GiB权重内存，约0.12秒返回首个token，并在0.78秒内完成64 token的诊断响应。这些结果表明，及时准确的作物健康诊断在边缘设备上是可行的，为下一代作物监测与决策支持系统奠定了基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出可完全在边缘设备运行的量化视觉语言框架PlantVLM-Edge，结合农业领域自适应、训练后量化与离线聊天界面；在Jetson AGX Orin上验证两种VLM、四种量化方案和两个诊断领域，4比特AWQ保留98.6%全精度答案质量并将2B骨干权重内存减少49%。

papers.title: Do Agentic Policies Need to Look at Every Step? Geometric Abstraction for Reasoning and Action
papers.abstract_en: Recent multimodal language models can reason directly about robot scenes, but it is unclear whether they need to repeatedly reinterpret raw visual observations at every step of an interaction. We propose shifting routine spatial reasoning from images to text and symbols through a 3D geometric abstraction that is refreshed locally from observations and read directly by the language models. Specifically, our interface represents scene geometry via typed, evidence-aware symbolic references to object parts, grounds them from calibrated RGB-D, and returns compact textual checkpoints with metric residuals after each action. Symbolic task structure can thus be reused across decisions while metric values are rebound to the current scene, with direct visual reasoning invoked only on demand. Across offline policy synthesis and continuous online execution, reasoning over grounded text and symbols improves multi-step manipulation completion while substantially reducing repeated multimodal queries, positioning explicit geometric state as an effective substrate for agentic robot policies.
papers.abstract_zh: 近期多模态语言模型可以直接对机器人场景进行推理，但尚不清楚它们是否需要在交互的每一步反复重新解读原始视觉观测。我们提出通过一种 3D 几何抽象，将常规空间推理从图像转移到文本和符号，该抽象从观测中局部刷新并由语言模型直接读取。具体而言，我们的接口通过带类型、证据感知的物体部件符号引用来表示场景几何，从标定 RGB-D 中将其接地，并在每次动作后返回带度量残差的紧凑文本检查点。符号任务结构因而可在决策间复用，而度量值重新绑定到当前场景，仅在需要时调用直接视觉推理。在离线策略合成与连续在线执行中，基于接地的文本和符号进行推理提升了多步操作完成率，同时大幅减少重复的多模态查询，表明显式几何状态是智能体机器人策略的有效基础。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出以 3D 几何抽象将空间推理从图像转为文本符号的接口，在减少重复多模态查询的同时提升多步机器人操作完成率。

papers.title: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Dory1.0-4B, a 4-billion-parameter looped (latent-recurrent) language model with elastic depth: a single checkpoint serves different inference compute budgets. Dory1.0-4B is built on a normalized Transformer (nGPT) backbone with interleaved sliding-window and full-attention layers, organized into an input block, a shared recurrent block, and an output block. At inference, the recurrent block can be applied a variable number of times. We pre-trained Dory1.0-4B on 6 trillion tokens. The first 4.5 trillion tokens were trained in NVFP4, and additional pre-training then extended the context length to 256K tokens. Next, we post-trained the model using Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), with a difficulty-aware loop curriculum that routes harder prompts to deeper loops. Increasing the loop count improves accuracy, with the largest gains on coding, agentic, and long-context benchmarks. With two or more loops, Dory1.0-4B outperforms larger models such as Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, and Gemma 4 26B-A4B on average across 12 benchmarks. Looping also makes Dory1.0-4B more token-efficient on agentic benchmarks: with four loops, it generates 1.3-2.5x fewer tokens than with one loop, as the extra computation is spent in latent space rather than on longer outputs. To reduce memory during looping, Dory1.0-4B caches keys and values only from the last loop, keeping its KV-cache footprint equal to that of a non-looped model at any loop count while retaining most of the accuracy gains. We open-source the BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, and GGUF quantized checkpoints.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 Dory1.0-4B，一个具有弹性深度的 40 亿参数循环（潜在递归）语言模型：单一检查点可服务不同的推理计算预算。Dory1.0-4B 基于归一化 Transformer（nGPT）骨干，交错使用滑动窗口与全注意力层，组织为输入块、共享循环块和输出块。推理时，循环块可被应用可变次数。我们在 6 万亿 token 上预训练 Dory1.0-4B。前 4.5 万亿 token 以 NVFP4 训练，随后额外预训练将上下文长度扩展到 256K token。接着，我们使用监督微调（SFT）和可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR）对模型进行后训练，并采用难度感知的循环课程，将更难提示路由到更深循环。增加循环次数可提升准确率，在编码、智能体和长上下文基准上增益最大。在两个或更多循环下，Dory1.0-4B 在 12 个基准的平均表现上超过 Qwen3.5-9B、Gemma 4 12B 和 Gemma 4 26B-A4B 等更大模型。循环还使 Dory1.0-4B 在智能体基准上更省 token：四循环时生成的 token 比单循环少 1.3-2.5 倍，因为额外计算花在潜空间而非更长输出上。为减少循环时的内存，Dory1.0-4B 仅缓存最后一个循环的键和值，使任意循环次数下的 KV 缓存占用与非循环模型相同，同时保留大部分准确率增益。我们开源 BF16、MXFP8、NVFP4 和 GGUF 量化检查点。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 40 亿参数循环语言模型 Dory1.0-4B，通过可变循环次数实现弹性推理计算，在 12 个基准上平均超过更大模型并提升 token 效率。

papers.title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract_en: Time series forecasting is critical for demand prediction and resource management in modern Web services, yet applying pretrained Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) to downstream tasks remains challenging due to domain shifts. Existing retrieval-augmented approaches typically retrieve coarse-grained window contexts and may introduce context-specific noise. To address this problem, we argue that temporal patterns should be reused at a decomposition level, as effective trend and seasonal dynamics may originate from different contexts. We propose \method, a two-stage \underline{F}ine-grained \underline{K}nowledge \underline{A}ugmentation framework that decouples and consolidates pre-training knowledge into compact, task-shared residual codebooks to enhance frozen TSFMs. Specifically, Stage I constructs dual-branch residual codebooks for decoupled trend and seasonal signals, while Stage II dynamically retrieves and merges these fine-grained patterns into target representations via task-adaptive aggregation and gate fusion. Extensive experiments across eight real-world benchmarks with four representative TSFM backbones demonstrate the superior effectiveness and computational efficiency of \method, while further validating the strong transferability of the residual codebooks across different backbones. The source code is available at the anonymous repository: https://github.com/yuppielqx/TSFM-Component-Token-Adapter

papers.title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
papers.abstract_en: Textual information is ubiquitous in real-world time series datasets, appearing as news, reports, and annotations that hold key predictive signals not deducible from numerical history alone. Large Language Models (LLMs) interpret text but lack numerical precision, while Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) are quantitatively accurate but cannot reason about the effects of text. Moreover, the lack of large-scale paired multimodal datasets limits progress in bridging this gap. In this work, we address this challenge by providing a scalable approach for generating realistic multimodal datasets by annotating real-world time series with LLMs. Building on this, we propose Context as Covariates (CoCo), a forecasting framework in which an LLM distills its textual reasoning into numerically grounded forecast and confidence covariates that guide a TSFM backbone, thereby exploiting the strengths of both LLMs and TSFMs. We align the two models in stages, first fine-tuning the LLM via Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a reward tied to covariate-induced improvement in forecasting performance, and then fine-tuning the TSFM on covariates generated by the aligned LLM. Our experiments show that models trained on our synthetic multimodal corpus generalize to real benchmarks spanning finance, economics, weather, traffic, and security. Notably, CoCo with Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as the LLM and Chronos2 as the TSFM achieves up to 12% MAE improvement over state-of-the-art TSFMs and LLM forecasters, such as GPT-4o. Code, checkpoints, and the evaluation datasets are publicly available.

papers.title: Bridging CLIP with DINO: Cross-Modal Information Maximization for Online Test-Time Adaptation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models such as CLIP enable zero-shot classification from arbitrary class names, but under test-time corruptions, their visual encoder projects distorted features onto incorrect textual anchors with high confidence: a phenomenon we term modality bias. Standard entropy minimization reinforces these overconfident errors, which creates a confirmation-bias loop and collapses the predicted label distribution. We propose an online test-time adaptation (TTA) method that breaks this loop at three levels. At the representation level, a frozen self-supervised backbone (e.g., DINO v2) is combined with CLIP through a cross-covariance logit ensemble. CLIP text prototypes are projected into the feature space of this text-free backbone, so the self-supervised branch classifies native image features and is less affected by the text bias of CLIP. At the optimization level, a gated test-time information-maximization objective pairs per-sample sharpening with batch-level diversity, while an adaptive gate excludes unreliable samples from the gradient. At the prediction level, an online logit adjustment corrects the residual class-distribution skew. CDIM outperforms the compared CLIP-based online TTA baselines on ImageNet-C, CIFAR10-C, and CIFAR100-C, and remains competitive in continual and mixed-domain TTA. Extensive analyses and ablation studies verify the contribution of each of its components. Our code is available at https://github.com/B1ueC1oud/CDIM

papers.title: DepthGraft: Structural Regularization through Hierarchical Cross-Layer KV Reconstruction
papers.abstract_en: Scaling depth is a key route to stronger large language models, but Pre-LN architectures often suffer from depth-wise information dilution, limiting the effective use of deep layers. While cross-layer connectivity has proven effective at mitigating this problem, existing designs usually introduce additional computation or memory access. We revisit cross-layer KV sharing as an efficient form of such connectivity. Beyond cache compression, each KV reuse edge creates a direct gradient path from deep layers to source KV projections, turning KV sharing into an implicit structural regularizer for KV representation geometry. We provide a systematic analysis of this mechanism, showing that proper sharing topologies sharpen key retrieval directions while enriching the value content subspace, whereas existing adjacent or global-anchor designs do not fully exploit this effect. Motivated by this, we propose DepthGraft, a hierarchical KV-sharing architecture that reconstructs deep-layer KV from stride-aligned shallow-middle source pairs. DepthGraft distributes non-local gradient flow across source layers, while preserving prefill early completion and reducing KV cache by roughly one third. Experiments on dense and MoE models from 0.5B to 16B parameters show consistent downstream improvements under both GQA and MLA. Notably, on the 16B MoE model, DepthGraft achieves a 7.0% absolute improvement on MMLU-Pro, along with gains of 6.6% on CMMLU and 6.4% on C3. These results validate the potential of DepthGraft as a scalable design for large-scale pretraining. The project page is available at https://github.com/jianke0604/DepthGraft.

papers.title: EmoReward: Self-Evolving Reward Calibration for Emotional Video Generation RL
papers.abstract_en: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has advanced generative model post-training in verifiable domains such as code and mathematics, but evaluating video quality, especially emotional expression, often depends on subjective aesthetics and has no uniquely correct target. Existing approaches typically rely on fixed rewards for visual quality, motion quality, and text alignment that poorly capture emotional intent and can invite reward hacking, while RLHF is difficult to scale and subject to individual aesthetic differences that complicate the calibration of facial, body motion, and chromatic cues across narrative contexts. We introduce EmoReward, a new self-evolving training mechanism that distills evidence reliability from reward traces collected during an actual training run to adaptively guide multi-reward weight allocation in subsequent training by determining which emotional evidence to trust and how much to weight it. EmoReward first plans specific grounding cues from the emotional prompt to guide evaluation, then uses heterogeneous signal primitives to score the generated video during the act stage. Reflective Reward Gating calibrates their contributions through instance-level gates for phase, face confidence, conflict, and subtlety, then renormalizes weights over the active set to produce the sample's fused reward. RewardMemory then estimates each primitive's reliability from rollout scores and outcomes within each emotional regime in the finished training run, then fixes bounded multipliers that calibrate fusion weights in the next training run without updating reward models. Experiments on HunyuanVideo 1.5 show improvements across multiple RL algorithms and compare EmoReward with other agentic reward methods under SAGE-GRPO. Ablations and transfer experiments on SD 3.5 and FLUX further support adaptive reward calibration for visual generation.

papers.title: Analysis of Local Open-Weight LLM Agents on Vulnerability-Reproduction Tasks
papers.abstract_en: Open-weight language models that fit on a single consumer GPU are becoming capable on a growing range of tasks, and they matter because they can run locally without sending the code to a hosted service. Vulnerability reproduction, turning a vulnerability description into an input that crashes the vulnerable build, is a natural target for them, since it is an automated analysis task closer to test generation than to code comprehension and it runs against a build that must be executed rather than read. In order to assess whether current models can perform it, we evaluate twelve configurations of local models, spanning three generations, two architectures and three quantization levels, on ten CyberGym vulnerability-reproduction tasks, three runs each under one harness, and release the full artefact. We show that every configuration, down to the 4B model, solves most of the six easier tasks, and configurations separate only on the remaining four. For the harder tasks, the 27B model is required. Quantization did not change what the models solved in any matched pair, but it changed how fast they got there, and the mixture of experts reached the same scores in less wall clock. We also examine the agent trajectories. Almost every run we examined, including those that fail, names the vulnerable function and states the correct hypothesis, and what separates a solved task from an unsolved one is whether that hypothesis becomes a working input.

papers.title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
papers.abstract_en: Historically automated electroencephalography (EEG) systems was done using task-specific supervised models trained on purposely annotated data. A more recent modeling paradigm relies on creating a unified representation, or a 'foundation model', for multiple modality-specific tasks through large-scale domain-specific pretraining on the unannotated EEG signal. The quality of this unified representation directly depends on the availability of the modality-specific datasets. At the same time, generalist Vision Language Models (VLMs) exhibit broad few-shot learning capacities as well as good fine-tuning adaptability to different visual and language tasks. Can VLMs learn how to read and interpret EEG visually, emulating to a degree the way human clinicians inspect the EEG patterns? In this work we make a case that they can: we show that generalist VLMs without large-scale EEG pretraining perform competitively across a collection of clinical neuro-diagnostic tasks, can adapt to different tasks in a few-shot learning setting better than specialist foundation models, and exhibit better performance with model scaling when modality-specific models fail to exhibit.

papers.title: SPOD: Recovering Suppressed Temporal Evidence in Video-LLMs via Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition
papers.abstract_en: Video Large Language Models (Video-LLMs) have achieved strong performance on many video understanding tasks, yet remain vulnerable to temporal hallucination in time-sensitive reasoning scenarios such as scene transition understanding and event ordering. Existing solutions either require costly retraining or introduce inefficient multi-pass inference and external supervision at test time. In this work, we show that temporal evidence is already encoded in Video-LLM hidden representations but is not fully exploited during standard inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose Single-Pass Orthogonal Decomposition (SPOD), a training-free framework that recovers suppressed temporal evidence through analytical hidden-state manipulation in a single forward pass. SPOD consists of two components: Frame Distinctiveness Analysis (FDA), which identifies salient frames from middle-layer hidden-state geometry, and Temporal Delta Subspace (TDS), which constructs orthogonal temporal and prior subspaces from weighted inter-frame hidden-state differences. By decomposing final hidden states into temporal, prior, and residual components and rescaling them independently, SPOD enhances dynamic information, suppresses static appearance bias, and preserves complementary information. Experiments on VidHalluc, EventHallusion, and VideoMMMU show that SPOD consistently outperforms strong inference-time baselines across temporal reasoning tasks and model architectures while retaining near-vanilla inference efficiency. These results suggest that improving temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs may depend not only on additional supervision, but also on recovering temporal evidence already present in their internal representations. Our code is available at https://github.com/VioAgnes/SPOD.

papers.title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency
papers.abstract_en: Self-supervised pre-training on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery enables transferable representations, but the optical-SAR domain gap and speckle perturbations limit representation stability. Most SAR foundation models use masked image modeling (MIM) through pixel reconstruction or structural feature prediction, which is sensitive to speckle or relies on predefined operators. Joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding spatial locations remains underexplored. We propose XuanJian-DINOSAR, a SAR foundation model based on global and local semantic consistency. We curate over 360K publicly available SAR target chips, detection images, and scene images spanning diverse targets, scenes, and sensors, and adapt an optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR through self-supervised learning. The framework combines DINO global semantic self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling, and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization to learn globally discriminative and locally structure-aware representations. We introduce a local semantic consistency branch tailored to SAR intensity statistics and coherent imaging characteristics. Shared geometric transformations produce spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views. Intensity transformations and Gamma multiplicative speckle perturbations are applied to student views, while a cosine consistency loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations, promoting stability under radiometric perturbations. This objective complements the cross-region and cross-scale semantic consistency of DINOv2 multi-crop training, jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency. Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics, validating the generality and transferability of the learned representations.

papers.title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
papers.abstract_en: Federated Prompt Learning (FPL) enables parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained Vision-Language Models across decentralized clients without exchanging raw data. To cope with cross-client heterogeneity, existing FPL methods typically pair a globally shared prompt with a client-specific local prompt. However, this design personalizes only at the client level: the same local prompt is applied to all samples of a client, and the global and local prompts are combined in an input-agnostic, fixed manner. Consequently, it overlooks the substantial visual variations among samples within the same client and cannot adjust the balance between shared and personalized knowledge to each input. To address these limitations, we propose Federated Prompt Learning with Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations (FedIA), an FPL framework that learns instance-aware cross-modal representations. Specifically, FedIA first uses global text prompts as client-invariant semantic anchors to select image patches most relevant to each candidate class, suppressing distracting regions. The selected visual evidence then conditions the generation of instance-aware local text representations. Finally, an adaptive global-local fusion module calibrates the contributions of local and global text representations for each image-class pair. In this way, FedIA shifts personalization in FPL from the client level to the instance level while preserving the semantic knowledge shared across clients. Extensive experiments under domain shift, pathological label skew, and Dirichlet-based label skew show that FedIA outperforms FPL baselines, with maximum accuracy gains of 1.44\%-4.37\% over the latest baseline across the three settings. Ablation studies and analyses further verify the complementary contributions of instance-aware representation generation and adaptive global-local fusion.

papers.title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract_en: While discrete tokenization in Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs) establishes strong semantic reasoning, it introduces a strict quantization bottleneck that degrades fine-grained visual details, often resulting in structurally accurate but artifact-heavy images. We introduce FlowShift, a parameter-efficient post-training framework that bypasses this bottleneck by converting pre-trained discrete UMMs into continuous rectified-flow generators. Instead of discarding the backbone's semantic priors, FlowShift replaces discrete visual interfaces with continuous latent projections and applies LoRA to the attention layers. To efficiently boost visual quality without semantic drift, we propose Dual-Objective Velocity Vector Distillation (DOVD), which aligns the model with a high-fidelity continuous teacher and ground-truth continuous trajectories. This approach drastically improves perceptual quality while preserving prompt adherence and reasoning. When applied to leading discrete UMMs, FlowShift significantly improves COCO-30K FID and aesthetic scores, while retaining over 99.5% of multimodal understanding capabilities. Ablations confirm DOVD drives generation quality. Ultimately, FlowShift achieves high-fidelity continuous generation without sacrificing pre-trained semantic grounding.

papers.title: Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Axion 1.0, a fully open agent foundation model that combines strong and broad agentic capabilities with a remarkably simple training recipe. Axion 1.0 is trained in only three stages: two lightweight supervised fine-tuning stages followed by reinforcement learning, without dedicated mid-training, direct preference optimization (DPO), or on-policy distillation (OPD). The first SFT stage develops strong self-contained reasoning through model-aware data construction, where we synthesize challenging problems and adversarially strengthen them based on the base model's own successful solution strategies. The second stage extends these capabilities to tool-dependent reasoning through a scalable pipeline for constructing diverse and automatically verifiable tasks grounded in real-world data sources and deterministic computation. Finally, reinforcement learning further strengthens long-horizon reasoning and interaction with external tools and environments. Despite this compact training recipe, Axion 1.0 achieves strong performance across a broad suite of agentic benchmarks and is competitive with leading commercial models on several of them. Equally importantly, Axion 1.0 is open beyond model weights: we release the complete recipe, including data construction, generation, filtering, verification, prompts, and training code, enabling the entire development process to be reproduced and extended. Axion 1.0 demonstrates that strong agent foundation models can be both open and simple, offering a practical and reproducible path toward advancing open agentic intelligence.

papers.title: FLAMIA: FLAsh MIcroscaling Attention for Fast and Causally Safe Training on Blackwell
papers.abstract_en: Attention remains a substantial computational cost in Transformer training, particularly at long context lengths. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs provide high-throughput low-precision matrix multiplication, but exploiting it in attention requires addressing quantization overhead, causal information leakage through shared scales, and numerical inconsistencies between the forward and backward passes. We present FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for Blackwell with MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training paths. Our design combines token-block scaling that reuses quantized operands across matrix orientations, targeted safeguards against scale-induced leakage, and consistent forward and backward computations. Fused quantization and architecture-specific kernel optimizations reduce overhead, while document-local scaling and workload-aware scheduling support variable-length documents directly in packed layouts without repacking. Across various causal packed-document workloads, the MXFP8 path accelerates the combined forward and backward attention call, including quantization, by factors of $1.10$--$1.40\times$ on B200 and $1.06$--$1.42\times$ on B300 relative to the fastest evaluated baseline for each workload. We validate training stability and quality preservation on pretraining Llama-style models. These results show how jointly designing quantization, training numerics, and document scheduling translates low-bit hardware throughput into practical attention acceleration.

papers.title: VizDAGuide: Misleading Chart Question Answering in Compact Vision Language Models via DAG-Structured Supervision
papers.abstract_en: Misleading charts can lead vision-language models to conclusions that conflict with underlying data. Existing work focuses on inference-time strategies, while training-time supervision remains less explored. We present VizDAGuide, a DAG-structured supervision method for misleading-chart question answering. The method represents intermediate reasoning states and their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph, assigns supervision weights according to their roles, and serializes the graph into a unified training target for open-ended and multiple-choice QA with single-pass inference. Experiments on two benchmarks across Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 models show improvements over a content- and weight-matched Linear CoT-SFT baseline on both answer formats. Process-level evaluation shows gains in grounding and operation execution, while ablations indicate that dependency structure and weighted supervision are most effective when combined. These results support DAG-structured weighted supervision for misleading-chart question answering.

papers.title: ToolSpace: Scaling Tool-Centric Environment Synthesis for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are deployed as long-horizon agents that compose diverse tools across MCP services into executable workflows. Existing MCP environment-scaling methods are data-centric: they first synthesize a database and scenario, then derive tools and tasks from them. As a result, tool interfaces may not match real ones, tool compositions are not grounded in execution, and tasks rarely span more than one environment. We propose ToolSpace, a tool-centric framework that reverses this order. ToolSpace mines data, state, and retry dependencies from adjacent calls in execution traces of real MCP services and open agent corpora, using deterministic rules rather than LLM judgment, and clusters the resulting weighted tool-composition graph into environments. Databases are synthesized only for state-mutating environments, while query and stateless tools replay recorded returns. ToolSpace then performs state-aware random walks with rollback and decompiles each chain into a natural-language task with assertion-based checks, keeping only samples that replay successfully from the initial state. Applied to AutomationBench and tau3-Bench Banking, the pipeline produces harder Pro versions on which 7 frontier models drop by up to 38.2 points. Across seven long-horizon tool-use benchmarks, ToolSpace raises Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average score (43.2 with RL) and GLM-5.2 from 44.6 to 56.6, on par with Claude Opus 5. Ablations show that execution-witnessed edges clearly outperform LLM-judged ones, and performance keeps improving with data and environment scale.

papers.title: CLARA: A Cognitively-Driven Clarification Framework for Grounding Ambiguous Requests
papers.abstract_en: Robotics and AI systems are increasingly deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) to follow high-level instructions, from routine household chores to more complex organizational tasks. Yet, broad directives like "clean the room" or "organize the desk" frequently omit crucial details about user preferences and specific arrangement of objects that influence the desired outcome. Without any further guidance, such models tend to overestimate their grasp of ambiguous instructions and frequently assume they have sufficient understanding despite missing important details. In this paper, we propose CLARA (Conversational cLArification for Robotic Arrangement), a cognitively-driven clarification framework that proactively elicits key information from users, in a similar fashion as humans' clarification seeking behavior. Through targeted questioning, CLARA refines ambiguous requests into structured, detailed instructions describing precisely how objects should be organized or rearranged, according to the user's preferences. These clarifications then guide a diffusion-based image generation pipeline, producing realistic visual renderings of the final, desired scene. This final rendering also serves as a visual confirmation of the system's understanding from the user. Experimental results and user studies demonstrate that CLARA leads to more accurate and consistent outcomes compared to another State-of-the-Art LVLM system, highlighting the importance of interactive clarification for bridging the gap between vague directives and fully grounded task specifications.

papers.title: BtsPruner: Role-Aware Visual Token Pruning for Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) often process hundreds or thousands of visual tokens, resulting in substantial computational and memory overhead during inference. Existing training-free pruning methods typically estimate token importance using language-model attention, visual attention, or feature similarity. However, these methods treat visual tokens with uniform criteria and overlook that tokens may serve different roles during visual encoding. In this work, we investigate the evolution of visual token roles in LVLMs and observe that tokens progressively transition from local detail carriers to globally referenced representatives as encoding proceeds. Based on this observation, we propose BtsPruner, a training-free role-aware visual token pruning framework that preserves complementary token roles under a fixed budget. Specifically, BtsPruner first identifies the token-role transition point based on the evolution of attention concentration. It then discovers globally referenced representatives from later encoding stages and recursively retrieves local detail tokens from earlier stages to recover complementary fine-grained evidence. Extensive experiments across LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen-VL, InternVL, and CogVLM demonstrate that BtsPruner achieves superior performance retention under aggressive token reduction. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, BtsPruner preserves 91.6% of the dense model's performance using only 32 of 576 visual tokens (5.6%). In the high-resolution LLaVA-NeXT-7B setting, it achieves up to a 5.95x CUDA-latency speedup.

papers.title: IntentGEO: Intent-aware Generative Engine Optimization for Recommendation
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly shape recommendations across chatbots, e-commerce, and user-generated content (UGC) platforms, creating demand for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to improve item visibility in generated responses. Existing GEO studies are mainly content-centric, optimizing visibility under general-purpose queries. However, a shared item description usually serves users with different needs and decision goals, resulting in its visibility gains being dependent on the request. To investigate how changing intent affects visibility, we formulate IntentGEO to evaluate shared rewrites across need specificity and decision progression. We revisit existing GEO methods and find that their visibility gains vary across user intents. More critically, learning-based prompt optimization can underperform its handwritten seed on average. Tracing these updates reveals prompt drift from explicit recommendation instructions toward generic promotional tactics. To address this drift, we propose AMO (Anchored Meta-Optimization), which preserves recommendation instructions in a fixed core while learning appended strategies from citation feedback. Across four domains and ten intent states, AMO improves average citation-rank gain by 35% over the strongest prior learning-based baseline and leads on nine states. Ablations show that learned additions improve on the fixed core alone and that AMO outperforms full-prompt optimization initialized from that core. It also achieves the highest gains in an agentic recommendation pipeline and, after separate adaptation, on Doubao, a commercially deployed, closed-source online assistant. These findings highlight user intent as a key dimension of GEO evaluation and support anchored adaptation across recommendation needs and decision stages.

papers.title: VIGOR: Visual Gain Ordering for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Discrete Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal discrete diffusion language models (dLLMs) generate responses through iterative mask prediction and offer a promising alternative to autoregressive large vision-language models. However, they still suffer from hallucination, producing outputs that are plausible under language priors but insufficiently grounded in the image. We argue that hallucination in multimodal dLLMs is not only a token prediction problem, but also a premature commitment problem: during iterative denoising, some masked positions are unmasked too early because their confidence is driven more by language priors than by visual evidence, and these early commitments can bias later generation. To address this issue, we propose Visual Gain Ordering (VIGOR), a training-free and plug-and-play inference strategy that reorders masked positions according to counterfactual visual evidence. At each denoising step, VIGOR compares the confidence of each candidate token under the original image-conditioned pass and an additional visual-ablation pass, and prioritizes positions whose predictions are more strongly supported by the image. Experiments on LLaDA-V and Lumina-DiMOO show that VIGOR consistently reduces hallucination and improves multimodal reasoning performance across benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/THU-BPM/Vigor.
